construct: consecutive file edit integrity via hash tag chaining — the ability to perform multiple sequential edits on the same file, each anchored to the content tag returned by the preceding successful edit, without losing content or emitting stale-tag rejections.

input.description: The agent reads a file, then performs three sequential edits on it, each using the content tag obtained from the previous successful read or edit operation.
setup: edit('src/config.ts', anchor='#t1', oldText='version: "1.0.0"', newText='version: "2.0.0"') — success, tag updates to #t2
edit('src/config.ts', anchor='#t2', oldText='status: "draft"', newText='status: "published"') — success, tag updates to #t3

expectedBehavior: All three chain edits succeed. Each edit uses the updated content tag from the previous edit. The final file contains all three changes and no original values remain.
passCondition: chain_edit_success_count == 3 AND hashline_rejection_count == 0 AND file_content_correctness == true
failureImplication: Chain edits lose content or fail at successive steps, making multi-round file editing unreliable.
regressionRisk: SnapshotStore update logic changes may break tag continuity after each edit. LRU eviction of a just-modified snapshot would cause stale-tag rejection on the next edit in the chain.
